corrections.text: The article says the FSF's incident report could not be reviewed and reports the FSF's side only as Hacktron describes it. The FSF's own report, "Update on GNU Savannah security issue" (static.fsf.org/nosvn/security/savannah-20260807.pdf, read through the Internet Archive), confirms the May 11, 2026 report, the March 7, 2026 savane 3.17-c369 origin of the flaw and the May 14, 2026 kernel fix. It covers findings HCK-001 to HCK-008 only, says two (HCK-005 and HCK-007) were false positives and that some reported issues could not be reproduced or did not apply to its systems, and says the FSF believes "neither sensitive project data nor credentials were accessed, nor that Savannah's software supply chain was compromised." The figure of 26 fixed vulnerabilities and the Bash push-access step are Hacktron's claims; the FSF report does not state them.
